detail:
The Ehlers-Danlos Society describes exercise as "the cornerstone of treatment" and cites "several high quality research trials in both children and adults" supporting physical therapy. Rather than generic strengthening, the described focus is on stabilizing muscles around hypermobile joints to provide dynamic stability, plus balance and proprioceptive training.

A 2019 randomized controlled trial with 24 patients found that closed-kinetic-chain plus proprioception exercises significantly improved knee proprioception, reduced pain, and improved quality of life.

Key principles from the Society: therapy should be individualized to the person; it is best done with a physical therapist who understands hypermobility; and aggressive stretching or "work hardening"-style repetitive forceful exercise should be avoided.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor or physical therapist before starting a new exercise program.
sourceVideoTitle: Evidence-based rationale for physical therapy treatment
